svg.title: One forward pass through microK3
svg.desc: A four-band architecture diagram. Band one traces the forward pass: bytes, token embedding, four layers (three Kimi Delta Attention layers then one gated global-attention layer, the first with a dense feed-forward and the rest with a Stable LatentMoE), a final depth mix, RMSNorm, and a tied language-model head. Layers never feed each other directly; each writes its contribution onto a growing depth bus and reads a learned softmax mix of the embedding and all earlier contributions. Band two details one block's internals, the KDA recurrent step with its constant-size state, the lower-triangular depth-attention pattern over five learned queries, and the Stable LatentMoE routing path with a shared full-width expert. Band three compares decoding memory (constant KDA state versus growing global key/value cache), the per-head Muon and AdamW optimizer split, and microK3's teaching scale against Kimi K3.
svg.text: the whole model on one page
Config(layers=4, dim=128, heads=4, experts=8, top_k=2, latent_dim=64, expert_hidden=192, dense_layers=1, vocab_size=256) · 1,645,496 params
every layer reads a learned mix of the embedding and all earlier contributions, then appends its own
x_i = Σ_j softmax_j( q_i · rmsnorm(source_j) ) · source_j
the bus grows left to right — layer i sees i + 1 sources, the output query sees all 5
its own contribution, not x + mixed + routed.

g.text: softmax runs over the lit cells

svg.text: DECODING · WHAT GROWS, WHAT DOES NOT
At T = 1,024 the one global layer caches 262,144 numbers;
the three KDA states together still hold 12,288.
